messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prefix-cache miss-rate spike detected for service=redwood-inference-frontend (us-west1). 5xxs up, tail latency +120ms across the board. Paging oncall. thread_ts=2178901234

alice_oncall: acked. i'm oncall and grabbing timeline. initial customer impact looks like higher latency for generate endpoints, some 503s reported. i'll post quick impact summary in a sec.

bob_sre: copy. i'm watching eviction metrics + prefix hit-rate. seeing a big surge in eviction_count starting ~12:08 UTC. cluster-wide.

carol_eng: logs-bot: i pushed a query for evictions and prefix invalidations: https://logs.redwood.internal/q/evict?from=2026-03-10T12:00Z&to=2026-03-10T13:00Z (internal)

dan_runtime: timeline note: we had a runtime config rollout at 12:02 UTC today (optimize/kv-ttl-change, sha=6a2f9b). the deploy was supposed to reduce prefix TTL for long-tail keys. rolling 25% completed by 12:05, full by 12:07.

alice_oncall: customer impact: ~4% of requests to /v1/generate saw >3s latency, sporadic 503s for a handful of enterprise customers pinned to us-west1. no data loss. flagging as P1 (degraded latency and error spike).

bob_sre: quick check: grafana panel: prefix_cache.hit_rate dropped from 94% -> 52% between 12:06-12:12. eviction_rate increased 8x. this looks like mass invalidation or aggressive TTL.

carol_eng: logs excerpt (repeating):
```
[2026-03-10T12:08:14Z] WARN evictor: evicting prefix=proj:abcd1234:embed due_to=over_capacity slots=4
[2026-03-10T12:08:14Z] INFO kv: cache_invalidate prefix=proj:abcd1234:embed reason=ttl_update agent=runtime-12
[2026-03-10T12:08:15Z] WARN evictor: evicting prefix=proj:efgh5678:embed due_to=over_capacity slots=5
```
This repeats many times.

dan_runtime: digging into the rollout: the change set included `kv.prefix_ttl_secs = 60` (was 3600). looks like the intention was to reduce memory pressure for stale long-tail prefixes, but that effectively made many prefixes expire almost immediately.

alice_oncall: that maps to the drop in hit-rate. can we roll back the runtime change?

bob_sre: rollback plan: revert kv.prefix_ttl_secs to 3600 and roll to 10% canary 1st. that should stop mass invalidations. doing canary now.

sre_erin: also consider mitigation: temporarily increase cache capacity for affected pool to give instant relief while rollback propagates. i can handle scaling.

carol_eng: shared traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace?id=abc123 (contains slow generate calls, shows repeated cache-miss on prefix lookup)

alice_oncall: applied mitigation: scaled cache pool `prefix-pool-usw1` +40% at 12:37 UTC. observing gradual increase in hit rate, tail latency improving.

bob_sre: rollback started at 12:42 UTC (reverted config commit 6a2f9b). canary 10% healthy. monitoring for eviction delta.

logs-bot: export available: https://logs.redwood.internal/export/2178901234/evictions-12-13.zip

dan_runtime: evidence summary:
- change 6a2f9b set kv.prefix_ttl_secs 3600 -> 60
- deploy finished 12:07 UTC
- eviction spike started ~12:08 UTC
- hit-rate drop and customer impact 12:09-12:30 UTC
- scale applied 12:37 UTC, rollback started 12:42 UTC, full rollback 12:50 UTC

carol_eng: additional signal: we saw a surge of `cache_invalidate` events with agent=runtime-12 and agent=runtime-14. agents correspond to canary and stage groups. suggests rollout produced uniform behavior.

pm_sam: customer note: support flagged three enterprise customers seeing elevated latencies; we've sent initial message and offered status updates. no SLA breaches yet but close — proactively looping account teams.

alice_oncall: post-rollback status at 12:56 UTC: hit_rate recovering back up to ~88%, error rate dropping toward baseline. keeping page open until stable for 30m.

bob_sre: hypothesis list (in-thread):
1) config TTL change caused mass invalidation -> observed in logs and timing. (Primary)
2) unrelated memory leak causing evictions (no memory OOM signals observed; less likely)
3) external process tripping on prefix naming collision (no evidence)
We should collect allocation metrics to be thorough.

carol_eng: i'm attaching the timeline CSV for the last hour (link): https://files.redwood/internal/timeline_2178901234.csv

alice_oncall: next steps / action items: 
- postmortem owner: bob_sre
- collect full grafana dashboards and snapshots (carol)
- correlate deploy lanes and rollout groups (dan)
- write customer-facing summary (pm_sam)

bob_sre: assigning myself as postmortem owner. i'll coordinate log collection and evidence attachment. expected prep: rough RCA draft in 24h, full write-up in 72h.

sre_erin: small operational note: add a gating step to future TTL rollouts (smoke test verifying hit-rate on small canary before full rollout). filing a follow-up PR template change.

alice_oncall: closing page note: system stable at 13:05 UTC, keeping incident channel open for RCA artifacts. thanks everyone for quick responses :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed (auto): severity downgraded to SEV3 at 13:08 UTC.

carol_eng: adding final attachments to thread: grafana-snapshots -> https://grafana.redwood/snapshots/prefix-hit-2178901234.png and commit diff -> https://git.redwood/optimize/commit/6a2f9b

bob_sre: leaving checklist: "verify no residual customer errors in last 24h" and "confirm rollback release notes for audit". i'll post the RCA link here when ready.

pm_sam: thanks all — will coordinate customer comms once RCA is done. :wave:
